npcs.name: Kerra Aldar
npcs.idle: Thirty sheep last spring. Nine now.

npcs.name: Tregarth the Hunter
npcs.idle: The moor is wrong this year. Even the wolves know it.

npcs.name: Old Hywel
npcs.idle: My grandfather's grandfather marched with the legion. Some of it, I think, is still marching.

npcs.name: Lieutenant Penhale
npcs.idle: Report to the commander if it's official. Report to me if it's strange.

npcs.name: Oath-Keeper Gerens
npcs.idle: Corineus wrestled the last giant off these cliffs. We swore we'd do it again if we had to. We have to.

npcs.name: Sergeant Jory
npcs.idle: New to Cornwall? Stay on the moor till you can hold a sword. Then stay on the moor anyway.

quests.title: The White She-Wolf
quests.offer:
Wolves took my flock - a few at a time, all spring, then twenty in one night. A white she-wolf leads them. I've seen her on the ridge, watching the fold.

I want her dead. I want her hide on my floor. Will you [hunt her]? Tregarth the hunter knows the moor - he'll tell you where she dens, even if he won't like it.
quests.summary: Kerra Aldar wants the white she-wolf that led the pack against her flock hunted down.

steps.text: The fold's torn open. But the tracks are wrong for hunting wolves - they come in running, from the west, as if something were driving them.

steps.goal: Ask Tregarth the hunter about the white wolf
steps.say: The white bitch? I know her. She's been on this moor eight years and never touched a sheep till this spring. Something's pushing the packs east - the [death stalkers] are out of the woods and hungry. Kill a few of those and see where the wolves go.

steps.goal: Hunt the death stalkers on the western moor
steps.text: Gorged, every one of them - and in the last one's den, a pile of small white bones. Wolf cubs. The she-wolf's den is close.
She's there. Thin as a rake, white fur gone grey with mud, standing over two cubs - all that's left of her litter. She doesn't run. She just watches you.

steps.say:
There she is. Followed you up.

She took Kerra's sheep, right enough. And she took them because the stalkers took her cubs and there was nothing else on the moor. Now the stalkers are dealt with. She'll go back west, or I'm no hunter.

Kerra asked for her hide. I won't do it for you. [Kill her], or [let her go].

options.say: ...Your call. Make it clean, at least.
Good. Go tell Kerra. She'll shout. Let her shout. She'll understand by spring.

steps.text: She doesn't fight much. The cubs run off into the heather.

steps.say:
You LET HER GO? I asked for -

...Death stalkers. Her own cubs. Gods. Tregarth told me the same and I wouldn't hear it.

Fine. FINE. If a single sheep goes missing, I'm coming to find you. Here - for the stalkers, if not the wolf.

She's dead? Good. Good.

Then why do I feel like this. Tregarth told me why she came. I wish he hadn't. Here. Take your reward and the hide - I don't want it on my floor after all.

mercy.text: For the stalkers, if not the wolf.

revenge.text: Take it. Take all of it.

quests.title: The Drowned Ninth
quests.offer:
Every autumn the drowned legion marches the old road south - ghosts, skeletons, whatever they are. Every autumn somebody from my family lays a wreath on their road. My grandfather's grandfather was one of them, so they say.

This year my grandson Kit laid it. He didn't come back. The [lieutenant] says it's not army business. Will you [find Kit]?

topics.lieutenant: Penhale. Young. Reads too much. He might listen.

quests.summary: Old Hywel's grandson Kit laid a wreath on the road where the drowned legion marches, and did not come home.

steps.goal: Ask Lieutenant Penhale about the legion
steps.say: Not official business, no. But I've read the old reports. The Ninth went into the marshes after a raiding king and never came out. They march the old road south every year, back to the barrow where their [centurion] lies. Anyone on the road goes with them.

steps.goal: Walk the legion's old road south
steps.text: The road is churned by hundreds of feet that left no prints. Skeletons in rusted mail stand guard along it, still at attention.
Kit's wreath, trodden flat. The tracks of the legion lead west across the moor - to the barrow of the giant dead.

steps.goal: Follow the legion west to the great barrow
steps.text: A giant skeleton stands at the barrow mouth holding a legion's eagle - and beside it, in a red cloak, a pale young man holding the standard pole. Kit.
The centurion's bones fall into a heap. The legionaries stop where they stand and kneel, waiting for an order.

stages.name: Centurion of the Drowned Ninth
stages.announce: The giant turns. 'Standard-bearer! Hold the line!' Kit doesn't move. The legion does.
stages.success: Centurion of the Drowned Ninth falls.

steps.say:
I couldn't put it down. The standard. I tried. They needed someone to carry it and I was there and I just... couldn't put it down.

It's lighter now. They're waiting. They're waiting for someone to tell them [what to do].

steps.goal: Decide what becomes of the legion's standard
steps.say:
The standard - the eagle. If we [lay it to rest] in the barrow with the centurion, I think they'll sleep. All of them. No more marching.

Or we [bring it home]. Grandfather would - gods, he'd weep. The Eagle of the Ninth, in our house. It's ours too, isn't it? Our family's?

options.say: You're right. You're right. Here - help me. ... There. Listen. Do you hear that? Nothing. Nothing at all.
Grandfather will never believe it. Come on. Let's go before they change their minds.

steps.goal: Bring Kit home to Old Hywel
steps.say:
He's home. And the legion's asleep - he says you laid the eagle down with them.

Four hundred years, that road. My family will still lay a wreath, mind. Out of respect. But we won't be going to find anyone.

steps.goal: Bring Kit home to Old Hywel
steps.say:
The Eagle of the Ninth. In my house.

...I heard marching last night, you know. Faint. Coming up the road from the marsh, where it's never come before. Kit hears it too. Take something, quick, before I change my mind about all of this.

quests.title: Bears on the Moor
quests.offer:
Welcome to the hardest corner of Albion. You'll want to start small. The young brown bears raid the Station's bins at night.

Will you [chase off the bears]? Stay on the moor near the Station - nowhere else is safe for you yet.
quests.summary: Young brown bears raid Cornwall Station's stores. A first task for a new arrival.

steps.goal: Chase off the young brown bears near the Station about 70 m north of Sergeant Jory

steps.say: Good. You're still alive. That's the first lesson of Cornwall.

quests.title: Spiderlings on the Cliffs
quests.offer:
Cliff spiderlings come up from the sea-cliffs north of the Station and spin over the paths. Small ones, for now. Their mothers live further west - don't go there.

Will you [clear the paths]?
quests.summary: Cliff spiderlings spin webs over the paths north of Cornwall Station.

steps.goal: Clear the cliff spiderlings about 220 m north-west of Sergeant Jory

steps.say: Paths are clear. You're learning. Lieutenant Penhale has something for you.

quests.title: The Watch on the Moor
quests.offer:
Moor wolves hunt in packs round the Station at dusk. They've learned we're soft-hearted. Teach them otherwise and you've earned your place at our fire.

Will you [stand the watch]? Then see Oath-Keeper Gerens - he'll tell you what Cornwall's really about.
quests.summary: Moor wolves hunt round Cornwall Station at dusk.

steps.goal: Drive off the moor wolves about 80 m north-west of Lieutenant Penhale

steps.say: That'll do. Welcome to Cornwall. Gerens is by the well - go and hear about giants.

quests.title: The Spider Mothers
quests.offer:
The spiderlings' mothers nest on the cliff tops west of here. Big as ponies. They're coming closer to the Station every season.

Will you [break the nests]?
quests.summary: Cliff spiders nest on the cliff tops west of Cornwall Station.

steps.goal: Kill the cliff spiders about 480 m west of Sergeant Jory

steps.say: The nests are broken? You're not new any more.

quests.title: Gorlois's Men
quests.offer:
The church on the cliff tops is haunted - every child in Cornwall knows that. They're Duke Gorlois's knights. The night Uther came to Tintagel wearing Gorlois's face - Merlin's doing - they died defending a duke who wasn't there.

They've started coming out. Will you [go to the church]? Tell them the truth, if they'll hear it.
quests.summary: The ghosts of Duke Gorlois's knights have started coming out of the Ghostly Church.

steps.goal: Get past the ghostly clerics about 280 m north-west of Lieutenant Penhale
Face Brother Jarrel, the church's dead priest
steps.text: Brother Jarrel lowers his hands. 'The duke came home that night. We saw him. We let him in.' He looks at you. 'It wasn't him, was it?'

steps.say:
He knows now. That's all any of them ever wanted - to know.

They say Merlin was sorry for that night. Not sorry enough.

quests.title: The Shrinking Folk
quests.offer:
The muryans are the old fae of Cornwall - every year a little smaller, till they're ants. This year they've turned spiteful. Their trickster says the giants promised to make them big again.

Will you [break the mound]? And catch the trickster.
quests.summary: The muryans, Cornwall's shrinking fae, have sided with the giants.

steps.goal: Break the muryans at their mound about 520 m south-west of Oath-Keeper Gerens

steps.text: The trickster squeaks: 'The giants were here first! Before Corineus! They'll make us big again!'

steps.say: Giants promising things. Corineus heard the same promises, and threw the one who made them off a cliff.

quests.title: The Bucca Storm
quests.offer:
The buccas - the sea-spirits of the fishermen - have come inland and they're angry. A storm's driving them out of the sea, they say, a white storm out of Lyonesse that isn't natural.

Will you [calm the buccas]? The only way they'll listen is after a beating.
quests.summary: The buccas, the fishermen's sea-spirits, have been driven inland by an unnatural storm from Lyonesse.

steps.goal: Beat the buccas into listening about 480 m south-west of Oath-Keeper Gerens

steps.say: A white storm out of Lyonesse. The white dragon's weather, the old women would say. I used to laugh at them.

quests.title: The Wolf Dens
quests.offer:
The white she-wolf's gone, but her pack has den mothers in the middle moor, and they breed faster than we can kill.

Will you [clear the dens]?
quests.summary: The moor wolves' den mothers breed in the middle moor.

steps.goal: Kill the moor den mothers about 600 m south-west of Kerra Aldar

steps.say: My flocks will see the spring. Thank you.

quests.title: The Old Beeches
quests.offer:
The beeches of the east wood are older than Corineus. The giants have been singing to them - and now the oldest have woken, and they walk west to join the giants.

Will you [fell the old beeches]? It grieves me to ask.
quests.summary: The oldest beeches of Cornwall have woken to the giants' singing.

steps.goal: Fell the aged beeches about 460 m south of Oath-Keeper Gerens
Fell the elder beeches walking west

steps.say: Felled. We'll plant again where they stood. Corineus planted the first of them, they say.

quests.title: The Rooters Dig
quests.offer:
Giant rooters - great boars - turning up the southern downs. They're not hunting, they're digging, in lines. The giants have them clearing ground.

Will you [stop the dig]?
quests.summary: Giant rooters dig the southern downs in lines, clearing ground for the giants.

steps.goal: Kill the giant rooters about 1.0 km south-west of Oath-Keeper Gerens

steps.say: Clearing ground for a road. The giants' road from Dartmoor. I knew it.

quests.title: The Ninth's Road
quests.offer:
Kit came home - thanks to you. But the Ninth still march. Every night, out of Cardova and along the road to the old fort, and back.

Why do they march? Will you [find out]?
quests.summary: The Drowned Ninth march every night from the Catacombs of Cardova to the old Roman fort and back.

steps.goal: Fight the legionnaires on the marching road about 830 m south-west of Old Hywel

steps.text: Under the breastplate, scratched into the bone: a giant's rune. 'DIG.' Someone has bound the Ninth to work.

steps.say:
Bound to dig? By giants? My grandfather said the Ninth marched into the mist two hundred years ago looking for a quarry they'd been promised.

They found it.

quests.title: Centurion Favius
quests.offer:
The Ninth's centurion, Favius, holds the old fort in the south-east and drives them out every night. He's the one the giants bound first.

Will you [break Favius]? Bring friends.
quests.summary: Centurion Favius drives the Drowned Ninth out of the old Roman fort every night.

steps.goal: Fight into the old Roman fort about 720 m south of Old Hywel

steps.text: Favius falls. 'The eagle,' he rasps. 'They took the eagle into Cardova. While they have it, we march.'

steps.say: The eagle. The legion's standard. As long as the giants hold it, the Ninth are theirs.

quests.title: The Eagle of the Ninth
quests.offer:
Favius told you: the giants hold the Ninth's eagle in the mouth of Cardova, and the legate guards it for them. Bring back the eagle and the Ninth can lie down.

Will you [take back the eagle]? Bring everyone.
quests.summary: The giants hold the Drowned Ninth's eagle at the mouth of the Catacombs of Cardova.

steps.goal: Go to the mouth of Cardova about 940 m south-west of Oath-Keeper Gerens
steps.text: The catacombs breathe cold. Torches, and the glint of gold on a pole.

steps.goal: Defeat the Legate of the Ninth
steps.text: The legate falls, and the eagle with him. Along the marching road, every legionnaire stops, and turns, and sits down.

stages.name: the Legate of the Ninth
stages.objective: Defeat the Legate of the Ninth
stages.announce: The legate of the Ninth raises the eagle on its pole: 'Legio IX Hispana! To me!' Behind him, the dead stand to.
stages.success: the Legate of the Ninth falls.

steps.goal: Bring the eagle to Oath-Keeper Gerens
steps.say:
The eagle of the Ninth. Two hundred years.

We'll bury it with honour at the Station. They were soldiers. They deserve that much.

quests.title: The Giant Graves
quests.offer:
In the west, the giants' own graves - the ones Corineus filled. Their skeletons are standing up, and they keep souls in cages round them.

Will you [free the captured souls]? Their keeper, Aricoer, is no friend to anyone.
quests.summary: Giant skeletons in the western graves keep captured souls in cages.

steps.goal: Break the giant skeletons about 1.0 km south-west of Oath-Keeper Gerens
Defeat Aricoer, keeper of the souls

steps.say: Freed. Corineus would be glad. He hated cages.

quests.title: The Quarry Road
quests.offer:
The giants have cut a road in the far south-west, down to Dartmoor - the quarry road. Every stone that went to Salisbury went up it. Every giant that comes north walks it.

Will you [break the road]? Bring the strongest friends you have.
quests.summary: Golestandt's quarry-giants hold the road from Dartmoor in the far south-west.

steps.goal: Fight the quarry-giants on the road about 1.5 km south-west of Oath-Keeper Gerens

clue.name: a giants' cairn of marked stones

steps.text: Marked stones, a giant's tally: so many for the Dance, so many for the causeway in the marsh, so many for 'the Sleeper's door'. At the bottom, a claw-mark, and one word in Albion: 'Dartmoor.'

steps.say:
Dartmoor. That's where it all comes from. The dragon in his lair, and his giants quarrying the moor to build his roads.

Corineus would have gone south. So should we, one day.

quests.title: Cirfans
quests.offer:
Cirfans, the great drake of the west, sits over the quarry road where it turns south. The giants feed him. He's the white dragon's own blood, they say - a grandchild.

If he falls, the road is ours. Will you [face Cirfans]? Everyone you can find.
quests.summary: Cirfans, the great drake of the west and Golestandt's grandchild, guards the quarry road.

steps.goal: Defeat Cirfans, the great drake of the west about 1.5 km south-west of Oath-Keeper Gerens
steps.text: Cirfans falls across the road, and the earth shakes - and far to the south, something enormous roars.

steps.say:
You heard that? That was Golestandt. He felt his grandchild die.

We can [carve the oath] on Cirfans' bones, so every giant who walks this road reads it. Or [send the head to Tintagel], so the whole of Cornwall knows the oath still holds.

options.say: Then carve it deep. 'Corineus threw the last one off the cliff. We are still here.'
Then it goes to Tintagel on a cart, and every village will turn out to see it pass.
